   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">1.</em></b></p> </td><td> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Description of Our Business</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Atlanticus Holdings Corporation (the "Company") and those entities we control.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We are a purpose driven financial technology company. We are primarily focused on facilitating consumer credit through the use of our financial technology and related services. We provide technology and other support services to lenders who offer an array of financial products and services, including private label and general purpose card products, to consumers who <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>have been declined by other providers of credit. Private label and general purpose card products are originated by The Bank of Missouri, WebBank and First Bank and Trust (collectively, our &#8220;bank partners&#8221;). Our bank partners originate these accounts through multiple channels, including retail and healthcare point-of-sale locations, direct mail solicitation, digital marketing and partnerships with <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In these Notes to Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements, "receivables" or "loans" typically refer to receivables we have purchased from our bank partners or from other <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We are principally engaged as a program manager, providing a technology platform and corresponding services to lenders in the U.S. to assist those lenders with offering products to consumers. These lenders pay us a fee and, in most circumstances, the lenders are then obligated to sell us the receivables they generate from these products. We acquire these receivables for the principal amount of the loan. For certain of our receivables, we also receive merchant fees from our retail partners that are used to enhance our returns for those receivables.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We compensate our bank partners monthly for the regulatory oversight they provide associated with our acquired receivables, the underlying accounts of which they continue to own and service. This compensation is based on both fixed and variable components dependent on the underlying performance of the acquired receivables (collectively, "Bank partner fees"). As we are obligated to compensate our bank partners for the duration of the underlying account, we recognize the fair value of these Bank partner fees within Card and loan servicing on the accompanying condensed consolidated statements of income on the date we acquire the underlying receivable.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We service the underlying receivables on behalf of our bank partners by providing and/or managing the ongoing customer service activities in the form of processing payments, providing regular notices of statement activity, and resolving customer complaints, billing disputes, and fraud claims. Our bank partners continue to own the underlying consumer accounts that they originate and provide regulatory oversight in the form of reviewing, approving the development of consumer finance programs and approving all related marketing materials, establishing the policies and procedures that govern the operation of the consumer finance programs, reviewing and approving customer complaint correspondence, performing ongoing compliance monitoring and testing and audits of the consumer finance programs, and providing settlement services between us and our retail partners. From time to time, we also purchase receivables portfolios from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties other than our bank partners. These products and services are reported through <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> reportable segments, Credit as a Service ("CaaS") and Auto Finance.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Within our CaaS segment, we apply our technology solutions, in combination with the experiences gained, and infrastructure built from servicing approximately <em style="font: inherit;">$52</em>&#160;billion in consumer loans over more than <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> years of operating history, to support lenders in offering more inclusive financial services. These products include private label credit cards using the Fortiva and Curae brand names as well as merchant associated brands. Private label credit products associated with the healthcare space are generally issued under the Curae brand while all other retail partnerships, including those in consumer electronics, furniture, elective medical procedures, and home-improvement use the Fortiva brand or use our retail partners&#8217; brands. General purpose credit cards use the Aspire, Imagine, Mercury and Fortiva brand names. Our flexible technology solutions allow our bank partners to integrate our paperless process and instant decisioning platform with the existing infrastructure of participating retailers, healthcare providers and other service providers. Using our technology and proprietary predictive analytics, lenders can make instant credit decisions utilizing hundreds of inputs from multiple sources and thereby offer credit to consumers overlooked by many providers of financing that focus exclusively on consumers with higher FICO scores. Atlanticus&#8217; decisioning platform is enhanced by artificial intelligence and machine learning, enabling fast, sound decision-making when it matters most.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We also report within our CaaS segment: <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) servicing income&#894; and <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) gains or losses associated with notes receivable and equity investments previously made in consumer technology platforms. These include investments in companies engaged in mobile technologies, marketplace lending and other financial technologies. <em style="font: inherit;">None</em> of these companies are publicly-traded, and the carrying values of our investments in these companies are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> material.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Within our Auto Finance segment, our CAR subsidiary operations principally purchase and/or service loans secured by automobiles from or for, and also provide floor plan financing for, a pre-qualified network of independent automotive dealers and automotive finance companies in the buy-here, pay-here, used car business. We purchase auto loans at a discount and with dealer retentions or holdbacks that provide risk protection. Also within our Auto Finance segment, we are providing certain installment lending products in addition to our traditional loans secured by automobiles.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><br/> &#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 11, 2025, </em>the Company acquired&#160;all&#160;outstanding equity interests of Mercury Financial LLC (&#8220;Mercury&#8221;), a leading data- and tech-centric credit card platform utilized by bank partners to provide credit cards to near-prime consumers in the U.S. The acquisition aligns with Atlanticus&#8217; strategic objective to expand its consumer credit offerings and increase scale within its credit card operations. At closing, Mercury became a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The acquisition was accounted for as an asset acquisition under ASC <em style="font: inherit;">805,</em> "Business Combinations" as substantially all of the fair value of the assets acquired were concentrated in a group of similar assets. Fair values of assets acquired and liabilities assumed were determined using management estimates and <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party valuations (e.g., replacement cost method).</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="c3182436" escape="true">
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></b></p> </td><td> <p style="font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif;"><b>Significant Accounting Policies and Condensed Consolidated Financial Statement Components</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">The&#160;following is a summary of significant accounting policies we follow in preparing our condensed consolidated financial statements, as well as a description of significant components of our condensed consolidated financial statements. The condensed consolidated financial statements furnished have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) and reflect all normal and recurring adjustments that are, in the opinion of management, necessary for a fair presentation of the results for the periods presented. The preparation of financial statements in accordance with GAAP requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities as of the date of our condensed consolidated financial statements, as well as the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during each reporting period. We base these estimates on information available to us as of the date of the financial statements. Actual results could differ materially from these estimates. Certain estimates, such as credit losses, payment rates, servicing costs, discount rates and yields earned on credit card receivables, significantly affect the reported amount (and changes thereon) of our Loans at fair value and certain Accounts payable and accrued expenses (carried at fair value),&#160;on our condensed consolidated balance sheets and condensed consolidated statements of income.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -37pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="c145072489" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -37pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Consolidation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The condensed consolidated financial statements include the accounts of the Company and its wholly owned subsidiaries. The Company&#8217;s policy is to consolidate the financial statements of entities in which it has a controlling financial interest. The Company determines whether it has a controlling financial interest in an entity by evaluating whether the entity is a voting interest entity or variable interest entity ("VIE") and if the accounting guidance requires consolidation. For more information on the Company's VIEs, see Note <em style="font: inherit;">7</em>&#160;"Variable Interest Entities".</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ReceivablesPolicyTextBlock" id="c145072490" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -36pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><b>Loans, Interest and Fees Receivable&#160;</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We&#160;maintain <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> categories of Loans on our condensed consolidated balance sheets: those that are carried at fair value (Loans at fair value) and those that are carried at net amortized cost (Loans at amortized cost). For our Loans at fair value (within our CaaS segment), we discontinue the recognition of interest and fees when the receivable becomes contractually <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> or more days past due. For our Loans at amortized cost (within our Auto Finance segment), we continue interest and fee billings until the time of charge-off if there is adequate value associated with the underlying asset serving as collateral for the receivable. Once a loan discontinues accruing interest and fees it is ineligible to return to accrual status. We charge off receivables underlying our Loans at fair value, against our Changes in fair value of loans, when they become contractually more than <em style="font: inherit;">180</em> days past due, or <em style="font: inherit;">120</em> days past due if they are enrolled in an installment loan product. We charge off our Loans at amortized cost receivables, against our Allowance for credit losses, when they become contractually between <em style="font: inherit;">120</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">180</em> days past due. For all of our receivables portfolios, we charge off receivables within <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> days of notification and confirmation of a customer&#8217;s bankruptcy or death. However, in some cases of death, we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> charge off receivables if there is a surviving, contractually liable individual or estate large enough to pay the debt in full.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><b>Loans at fair value.</b></i>&#160;Loans at fair value represent receivables for which we have elected the fair value option (the "Fair Value Receivables"). The Fair Value Receivables are held by entities that qualify as VIEs, and are consolidated onto our condensed consolidated balance sheets, some portfolios of which are unencumbered and some of which are still encumbered under structured or other financing facilities. Loans and finance receivables include accrued and unpaid interest and fees. All receivables associated with private label credit and general purpose credit cards are included within this category of receivables.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>
    <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Under&#160;the fair value option, fees such as annual fees are taken into income when billed to the consumer or upon loan acquisition and any cost associated with the loan acquisition are expensed in the period incurred. The Company estimates the fair value of the loans using a discounted cash flow model, which considers various unobservable inputs such as credit losses, payment rates, servicing costs, discount rates and yields earned on credit card receivables. The Company reevaluates the fair value of loans receivable at the close of each measurement period. Changes in the fair value of loans are recorded as a component of "Changes in fair value of loans" in the condensed consolidated statements of income in the period of the fair value changes. Changes in the fair value of loans include the impact of current period charge-offs associated with these receivables.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Further details concerning our loans at fair value are presented within Note <em style="font: inherit;">6,</em> "Fair Values of Assets and Liabilities."</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><b>Loans at amortized cost, net.</b></i> Our loans at amortized cost, net, currently consist of receivables associated with our Auto Finance segment&#8217;s operations and are presented in the condensed consolidated balance sheets net of the related allowance for credit losses and deferred revenue. We purchased auto loans with outstanding principal of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145068653" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireLoansAndLeasesHeldForInvestment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">50.7</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145068654" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireLoansAndLeasesHeldForInvestment" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">48.1</ix:nonFraction> million for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> respectively, through our prequalified network of independent automotive dealers and automotive finance companies.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We show an allowance for credit losses for our loans at amortized cost. A considerable amount of judgment is required to assess the ultimate amount of expected losses on loans at amortized cost, and we regularly evaluate and update our methodologies to determine the most appropriate allowance necessary. Our loans at amortized cost consist of smaller-balance, homogeneous loans in our Auto Finance segment. These loans are further divided into pools based on common characteristics such as contract or acquisition channel. For each pool, we determine the necessary allowance for credit losses using reasonable and supportable forecasts that analyze some or all of the following attributes unique to each type of receivable pool: historical loss rates on similar loans&#894; current delinquency and roll-rate trends which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>indicate consumer loss rates in excess or less than those which historical trends might suggest&#894; the effects of changes in the economy on consumers such as inflation or other macroeconomic changes&#894; changes in underwriting criteria&#894; unfunded commitments (to the extent they are unconditional), and estimated recoveries. The aforementioned inputs are calculated using historical trends over the most recent <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> year period, and adjusted as needed for current trends and reasonable and supportable forecasts. We <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>individually evaluate a receivable or pool of receivables for credit losses if circumstances indicate that the receivable or pool of receivables <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be at higher risk for non-performance than other receivables (e.g., if a particular retail or auto-finance partner has indications of nonperformance (such as a bankruptcy) that could impact the underlying pool of receivables we purchased from the partner).</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Certain of our loans at amortized cost also contain components of deferred revenue related to loan discounts on the purchase of our auto finance receivables. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> March&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em>the weighted average remaining accretion period for the $<ix:nonFraction id="c145068662" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableDeferredIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">19.5</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145068663" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableDeferredIncome" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">20.1</ix:nonFraction> million of deferred revenue reflected in the condensed consolidated balance sheets was <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="atlc:WeightedAverageRemainingAccretionPeriodOfDeferredRevenue" id="c145068664" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">21</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;and <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" name="atlc:WeightedAverageRemainingAccretionPeriodOfDeferredRevenue" id="c145068665" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">23</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;months, respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Delinquent loans at amortized cost reflect the principal, fee and interest components of loans we did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> collect on or prior to the contractual due date and are considered "past due". Amounts we believe we will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> ultimately collect are included as a component in our overall allowance for credit losses.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We consider loan delinquencies a key indicator of credit quality because this measure provides the best ongoing estimate of how a particular class of receivables is performing. An aging of our delinquent loans at amortized cost (in millions) as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026&#160;</em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025&#160;</em>is as follows:</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b>Loan Modifications and Restructurings</b></i></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-indent: 36pt;">
    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;">We&#160;review our Loans at amortized cost, net, associated with our Auto Finance segment&#8217;s operations to determine if any modifications for borrowers experiencing financial difficulty were made that would qualify the receivable as a Financial Difficulty Modification ("FDM"). This could include a restructuring of the loan terms to alleviate the burden of the borrower's near-term cash requirements, such as a modification of terms to reduce or defer cash payments to help the borrower attempt to improve its financial condition. For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>&#160;months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026&#160;</em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em>&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">no</em> Loans at amortized cost qualified as a FDM.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c145072492" escape="true"><p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i><b>Income Taxes</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We experienced effective tax rates of <ix:nonFraction id="c145068684" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">24.4</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction id="c145068685" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:EffectiveIncomeTaxRateContinuingOperations" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">23.6</ix:nonFraction>% for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">These effective tax expense rates were above the statutory rate principally due to (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) state and foreign income tax expense, (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) deduction disallowance under Section <em style="font: inherit;">162</em>(m) of the Internal Revenue Code of <em style="font: inherit;">1986,</em> as amended, with respect to compensation paid to our covered employees, and (<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) taxes on global intangible low-taxed income. Offsetting the foregoing items were deductions associated with the vesting of restricted stock at times when the fair value of our stock exceeded such share-based awards&#8217; grant date values. Another offsetting item in only the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2025, </em>was our deduction of interest expense on a financial instrument classified as debt for tax purposes that was repaid in the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, </em><em style="font: inherit;">2025&#8212;such</em> financial instrument which was characterized in our consolidated financial statements as dividend-paying preferred stock.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We report interest expense associated with our income tax liabilities (including accrued liabilities for uncertain tax positions to the extent such liabilities have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been favorably resolved thereby resulting in interest expense reversals) within our income tax line item on our consolidated statements of income. Such interest expense was de minimis in both the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" id="c145072493" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><b><i>Revenue Recognition and Revenue from Contracts with Customers</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Consumer Loans, Including Past Due Fees</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Consumer loans, including past due fees reflect interest income, including finance charges, and late fees on loans in accordance with the terms of the related customer agreements. These fees are recognized when assessed based upon the contractual terms of the loans. Discounts received associated with auto loans that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included as part of our Fair Value Receivables are deferred and amortized over the average life of the related loans using the effective interest method. Finance charges and fees, net of amounts that we consider uncollectible, are included in loans, interest and fees receivable and revenue when the fees are earned based upon the contractual terms of the loans. Retail partner incentives such as fee reductions or rebates are recorded as a reduction to revenue over the period the incentives are earned.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Merchant fees paid or received associated with the acquisition of Fair Value Receivables are recognized when the merchant confirms the transaction with us, which fulfills the terms of the associated merchant agreement. Our merchant agreements are defined at the transaction level and do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> extend beyond the service already provided (i.e., each transaction is separate). We independently negotiate each agreement with separate counterparties and consider ourselves the principal in each agreement with our bank partners and retail partners. As such, we view the economic substance of our relationship with our retail partners as a service contract. The merchant fee is derived based on the value of the goods purchased from our retail partners and considers factors such as the consumer&#8217;s credit risk and the terms of our bank partners' related product offering.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our service comprises a single performance obligation to facilitate the transaction between the retail partner and its consumer and the merchant fee is recognized into income when the retail partner successfully confirms the transaction, as <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> remaining obligations exist under the contract.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Fees and Related Income on Earning Assets</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Fees and related income on earning assets primarily include fees associated with credit products such as annual fees, cash advance fees, and other fees. These fees are assessed based upon the contractual terms of the loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We recognize these fees as income when they are billed to the customers&#8217; accounts. Fees and related income on earning assets, net of amounts that we consider uncollectible, are included in loans, interest and fees receivable and revenue when the fees are earned based upon the contractual terms of the loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Other</i></b>&#160;<b><i>revenue</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Other revenue includes revenue from contracts with customers, which includes interchange revenues, servicing income, service charges and other customer related fees. We recognize these fees as income in the period earned.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;"><b><i>Other non-operating income</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Other non-operating income includes income (or loss) associated with investments in non-core businesses or other items <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> directly associated with our ongoing operations. <em style="font: inherit;">None</em> of these companies are publicly-traded and there are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material pending liquidity events. We will continue to carry the investments on our books at cost minus impairment, if any, plus or minus changes resulting from observable price changes.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i><b>Revenue from Contracts with Customers</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The majority of our revenue is earned from financial instruments and is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> included within the scope of ASC <em style="font: inherit;">606,</em> "Revenue from Contracts with Customers". We have determined that revenue from contracts with customers would primarily consist of merchant fees and interchange revenues in our CaaS segment and servicing revenue and other customer-related fees in both our CaaS segment and our Auto Finance segment. Interchange fees are earned when our customers&#8217; cards are used over established card networks. We earn a portion of the interchange fee the card networks charge merchants for the transaction and these fees are settled daily. Additionally, within interchange revenues are network incentives which are earned when credit card transactions, associated with accounts we service, are processed through interchange networks. Servicing revenue is generated by meeting contractual performance obligations related to the collection of amounts due on receivables, and is settled with the customer net of our fee, which can be settled daily or monthly. Service charges and other customer related fees are earned from customers based on the occurrence of specific services and are paid by customers per the terms of their credit agreement. Merchant fees paid or received associated with the acquisition of Fair Value Receivables are recognized when the merchant confirms the transaction with us, which fulfills the terms of the associated merchant agreement. <em style="font: inherit;">None</em> of these revenue streams result in an ongoing obligation beyond what has already been rendered. Revenue from these contracts with customers is included in Consumer loans, including past due fees and Other revenue on our condensed consolidated statements of income. Components (in thousands) of our revenue from contracts with customers is as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><i><b></b></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c145072494" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt;"><i><b>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</b></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11,</em> <i>Interim Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>): Narrow-Scope Improvements</i>. The ASU clarifies existing interim disclosure requirements and establishes a principle requiring entities to disclose events that occur after the end of the most recent annual reporting period that have a material impact on the entity. The new guidance is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>and interim periods within those annual reporting periods. Early adoption is permitted. The amendments are applied prospectively. We are currently evaluating the potential impact of adopting this new guidance on our financial statements and disclosures but the new guidance is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a significant impact to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements when adopted.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -2pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08,</em> <i>Financial Instruments</i>&#8212;<i>Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Purchased Loans</i>. The ASU requires purchased seasoned loans to be accounted for using a gross-up approach, which is intended to enhance comparability in accounting for acquired financial assets. The guidance is effective for public business entities for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>including interim periods within those annual reporting periods. Early adoption is permitted. We are currently evaluating the potential impact of adopting this new guidance on our financial statements and disclosures but the new guidance is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a significant impact to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements when adopted.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 5pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05,</em> "Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets", which improves transparency to provide all entities with a practical expedient when estimating expected credit losses for current accounts receivable and current contract assets arising from transactions accounted for under Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606.</em> All entities <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>elect a practical expedient that assumes that current conditions as of the balance sheet date do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> change for the remaining life of the asset. The new guidance is effective for fiscal years beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2025, </em>and interim reporting periods within those annual periods. We adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05</em>&#160;for the period ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026, </em>and elected the practical expedient.&#160;Adoption of this standard did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material effect on our condensed consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 5pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> "Income Statement&#8212;Reporting Comprehensive Income&#8212;Expense Disaggregation Disclosures" which requires disaggregated disclosure of income statement expenses for public business entities. The ASU does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> change the expense captions an entity presents on the face of the income statement. Instead, it requires disaggregation of certain expense captions into specified categories in disclosures within the footnotes to the financial statements. The amendments in this Update are effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027 </em>and early adoption of the amendments is permitted. We are currently evaluating the potential impact of adopting this new guidance on our financial statements and disclosures but the new guidance is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a significant impact to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements when adopted.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 5pt; text-indent: 36pt;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3182444" escape="true">
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top;"><td style="width: 36pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">3.</em></b></p> </td><td> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Segment Reporting</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We operate primarily within <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> industry consisting of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145068878">two</span> reportable segments by which we manage our business. Our <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145068879">two</span> reportable segments are: CaaS and Auto Finance. The Company defines operating segments to be components of the Company for which discrete financial information is evaluated regularly by the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer (our chief operating decision maker, "CODM") to allocate resources and evaluate financial performance. The CODM uses GAAP Income before income taxes to evaluate segment profitability as it provides the best insight into the segments overall economic performance. Income before income taxes is used regularly in the forecasting and budgeting process when assessing performance on a quarterly basis and making decisions about capital and personnel allocations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our CaaS segment includes the operations of <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145068880">three</span> operating segments aggregated into <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> reportable segment which includes our private label credit, our general purpose credit card receivables and those general purpose credit card receivables acquired as part of our acquisition of Mercury, all of which, through our bank partners, provide financing solutions to consumers. Our Auto Finance reportable segment purchases and/or service loans secured by automobiles and provides other financing options to independent automotive dealers and automotive finance companies. These <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c145068882">two</span> reportable segments were determined by management based on the characteristics of the underlying products, management structures and expected returns.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We have <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material amounts of long lived assets located outside of the U.S. and all revenue is generated within the U.S.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">We measure the profitability of our reportable segments based on their income after allocation of specific costs and corporate overhead (Income before income taxes)&#894; however, our segment results do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reflect any charges for internal capital allocations among our segments. Company revenues, expenses and profitability are aggregated into these segments and presented to the CODM as detailed below. Overhead costs are allocated based on headcounts and other applicable measures to better align costs with the associated revenues. Income taxes are allocated to the individual segments whereby each operating segment determines income tax expense or benefit as if it filed a separate tax return.</p>
   <p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;text-indent:36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 26, 2014, </em>we and certain of our subsidiaries entered into a Loan and Security Agreement with Dove Ventures, LLC, a Nevada limited liability company ("Dove"). The agreement provided for a senior secured term loan facility in an amount of up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069078" contextRef="i_2014-11-26_CreditFacilityAxis-SeniorSecuredTermLoanFacilityMember_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-DoveVenturesLLCMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LineOfCreditFacilityMaximumBorrowingCapacity" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">40.0</ix:nonFraction> million at any time outstanding. On <em style="font: inherit;"> December 27, 2019, </em>the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c145069079" contextRef="i_2019-12-27_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:TemporaryEquitySharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">400,000</ix:nonFraction> shares of its Series A Preferred Stock with an aggregate initial liquidation preference of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069080" contextRef="i_2019-12-27_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:TemporaryEquityLiquidationPreference" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">40.0</ix:nonFraction> million, in exchange for full satisfaction of the $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069081" contextRef="d_2019-12-27_2019-12-27_CreditFacilityAxis-SeniorSecuredTermLoanFacilityMember_RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis-DoveVenturesLLCMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ExtinguishmentOfDebtAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">40.0</ix:nonFraction> million that the Company owed Dove under the Loan and Security Agreement. Dividends on the preferred stock are <ix:nonFraction id="c145069082" contextRef="d_2019-12-27_2019-12-27_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockDividendRatePercentage" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">6</ix:nonFraction>% per annum (cumulative, non-compounding) and are payable as declared, and in preference to any dividends on common stock and Series B preferred stock, in cash. The Series A Preferred Stock is perpetual and has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> maturity date. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may, </em>at its option, redeem the shares of Series A Preferred Stock at a redemption price equal to $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069084" contextRef="i_2019-12-27_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:TemporaryEquityRedemptionPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">100</ix:nonFraction> per share, plus any accumulated and unpaid dividends. At the request of holders of a majority of the shares of Series A Preferred Stock, the Company shall offer to redeem all of the Series A Preferred Stock at a redemption price equal to <em style="font: inherit;">$100</em> per share, plus any accumulated and unpaid dividends, at the option of the holders thereof. Upon the election by the holders of a majority of the shares of Series A Preferred Stock, each share of the Series A Preferred Stock is convertible into the number of shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock as is determined by dividing (i) the sum of (a) <em style="font: inherit;">$100</em> and (b) any accumulated and unpaid dividends on such share by (ii) an initial conversion price equal to $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069087" contextRef="i_2019-12-27_StatementClassOfStockAxis-SeriesAPreferredStockMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="atlc:TemporaryEquityConversionPricePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">10</ix:nonFraction> per share, subject to certain adjustment in certain circumstances to prevent dilution. Given the redemption rights contained within the Series A Preferred Stock, we account for the outstanding preferred stock as temporary equity in the condensed consolidated balance sheets. Dividends paid on the Series A Preferred Stock are deducted from Net income attributable to controlling interests to derive Net income attributable to common shareholders. The common stock issuable upon conversion of Series A Preferred Stock is included in our calculation of Net income attributable to common shareholders per share&#8212;diluted. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">11,</em> "Net Income Attributable to Controlling Interests Per Common Share" for more information.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Dove is a limited liability company owned by <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> trusts.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> November 14, 2019, </em>a wholly-owned subsidiary issued <ix:nonFraction id="c145069093" contextRef="i_2019-11-14_PreferredUnitsByNameAxis-ClassBPreferredUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:PreferredUnitsIssued" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">50.5</ix:nonFraction> million Class B preferred units at a purchase price of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069094" contextRef="i_2019-11-14_PreferredUnitsByNameAxis-ClassBPreferredUnitsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="atlc:PreferredUnitPurchasePrice" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.00</ix:nonFraction> per unit to an unrelated <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. The units carried&#160;a <ix:nonFraction id="c145069096" contextRef="i_2019-11-14_PreferredUnitsByNameAxis-ClassBPreferredUnitsMember" unitRef="Pure" name="atlc:PreferredUnitsIssuedPercentageOfPreferredReturn" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">16</ix:nonFraction>% preferred return to be paid quarterly. In <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2020, </em>the subsidiary issued an additional <ix:nonFraction id="c145069097" contextRef="d_2020-03-01_2020-03-31_PreferredUnitsByNameAxis-ClassBPreferredUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="atlc:AdditionalPreferredUnitsIssued" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">50.0</ix:nonFraction> million Class B preferred units under the same terms. The proceeds from the transaction were used for general corporate purposes. During the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024, </em>we redeemed <ix:nonFraction id="c145069098" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_PreferredUnitsByNameAxis-ClassBPreferredUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="atlc:PreferredUnitsSharesRedeemedDuringPeriod" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">50.5</ix:nonFraction> million of the Class B preferred units at $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069099" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_PreferredUnitsByNameAxis-ClassBPreferredUnitsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="atlc:PreferredUnitsRedemptionPricePerUnit" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.00</ix:nonFraction> per unit plus accrued but unpaid interest thereon. In <em style="font: inherit;"> March&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> we redeemed the remaining <ix:nonFraction id="c145069101" contextRef="d_2025-03-01_2025-03-31_PreferredUnitsByNameAxis-ClassBPreferredUnitsMember" unitRef="Share" name="atlc:PreferredUnitsSharesRedeemedDuringPeriod" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">50.0</ix:nonFraction> million of Class B preferred units at $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069102" contextRef="d_2025-03-01_2025-03-31_PreferredUnitsByNameAxis-ClassBPreferredUnitsMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="atlc:PreferredUnitsRedemptionPricePerUnit" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.00</ix:nonFraction> per unit plus accrued but unpaid interest thereon. In periods where present, we have included the issuance of these Class B preferred units as temporary noncontrolling interest on the condensed consolidated balance sheets. Dividends paid on the Class B preferred units were deducted from Net income attributable to controlling interests to derive Net income attributable to common shareholders. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">11,</em> "Net Income Attributable to Controlling Interests Per Common Share" for more information.</p>

  <div>
    &#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3182449" escape="true">
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 36pt; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;"><b><em style="font: inherit;">6.</em></b></p> </td><td style="font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;"><b>Fair Values of Assets and Liabilities</b></p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received for an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants on the measurement date.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;">We update our fair value analysis each quarter, with changes since the prior reporting period reflected as a component of "Changes in fair value of loans" in the condensed consolidated statements of income. Changes in yields, purchase and payment rates, servicing rates, realized and projected credit loss rates and discount rates will lead to changes in the fair value of loans and therefore impact earnings. Further, our retail asset typically has seasonal growth during the summer months, impacting the fair value of assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;">Fair value differs from amortized cost accounting in the following ways:</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 36pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">Receivables are recorded at their fair value, <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> their principal and fee balance or cost basis&#894;</td></tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 36pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">The fair value of the loans takes into consideration net charge-offs for the remaining life of the loans with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> separate allowance for credit loss calculation&#894;</td></tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 36pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">Certain fee billings (such as non-refundable annual fees) and expenses of loans are <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer deferred but recognized (when billed or incurred) in income or expense, respectively&#894;</td></tr>
<tr><td style="width: 36pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">The net present value of cash flows associated with future fee billings on existing receivables are included in fair value&#894;</td></tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 36pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">Changes in the fair value of loans impact net margins&#894; and</td></tr>
<tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 36pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</td><td style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt;">Net charge-offs are recognized as they occur rather than through the establishment of an allowance and provision for credit losses for those loans, interest and fees receivable carried at amortized cost.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt -2pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt -2pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">For&#160;receivables that are carried at net amortized cost, we include disclosures of the fair value of such receivables to the extent practicable within the disclosures below.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt -2pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt -2pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">Where applicable, we account for our financial assets and liabilities at fair value based upon a <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-tiered valuation system. In general, fair values determined by Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs use quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that we have the ability to access. Fair values determined by Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> inputs use inputs other than quoted prices included in Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> inputs include quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, and inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability, such as interest rates and yield curves that are observable at commonly quoted intervals. Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs are unobservable inputs for the asset or liability, and include situations where there is little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability. Where inputs used to measure fair value <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>fall into different levels of the fair value hierarchy, the level in the fair value hierarchy within which the fair value measurement in its entirety has been determined is based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement in its entirety.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt -2pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt -2pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">Our&#160;assessment of the significance of a particular input to the fair value measurement in its entirety requires judgment and considers factors specific to the asset or liability.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;">For&#160;those asset classes above that are carried at fair value in our condensed consolidated financial statements, gains and losses associated with fair value changes are detailed on our condensed consolidated statements of income as a component of Changes in fair value of loans. Variations in the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> month U.S. Treasury bill rate over the measurement period are used to determine the portion of change in fair value considered to be attributable to changes in instrument-specific credit risk. These variations are applied to the period end discount rate we use to determine fair value. For our loans included in the above table, we assess the fair value of these assets based on our estimate of future cash flows net of servicing costs. For the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026&#160;</em>and <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em> we estimate the portion of fair value changes considered to be attributable to changes in instrument-specific credit risk to be $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069125" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FairValueOptionCreditRiskGainsLossesOnAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12.1</ix:nonFraction> million and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145069126" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-03-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FairValueOptionCreditRiskGainsLossesOnAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">9.3</ix:nonFraction> million, respectively.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">The&#160;unrealized gains and losses for assets within the Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> category presented in the tables above include changes in fair value that are attributable to both observable and unobservable inputs.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; text-indent: 36pt;"><i><b>Loans at Fair Value.</b></i>&#160;The fair value of Loans at fair value is based on the present value of future cash flows using a valuation model of expected cash flows and the estimated cost to service and collect those cash flows. We estimate the present value of these future cash flows using internally-developed estimates of assumptions <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party market participants would use in determining fair value, including estimates of credit losses, payment rates, servicing costs, discount rates and yields earned on private label credit and general purpose credit card receivables. We forecast the cash flows underlying our fair value assessment based on the individual offer type (in the case of general purpose credit cards) or by specific offers at our retail partners (for private label credit). While overall product return requirements among the offer types <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be similar, the individual product offerings necessary to achieve those returns is often unique to each offer and retailer based on several factors, including acceptance rates of the offers by consumers and underlying consumer performance data which varies by offer type.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">Our fair value models include market degradation to reflect the possibility of delinquency rates increasing in the near term (and the corresponding increase in charge-offs and decrease in payments) above the level that current trends would suggest.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">The fair value of loans we acquire associated with our retail partners are typically lower than the aggregate unpaid gross balance of the underlying loans due to loan originations by our bank partners that contain below market interest rates or fees charged to consumers. Under agreements with our bank partners, we are required to purchase these receivables for amounts that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be in excess of fair value. In these instances, a fair value assessment that is less than the purchase price of the receivable can occur on the date we initially acquire the receivable, resulting in a loss on acquisition of the receivable. This negative fair value assessment is included in Changes in fair value of loans on our condensed consolidated statements of income.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -9pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt -1pt; text-indent: 36pt;">In cases where we acquire receivables below market rates, we charge merchant fees to our retail partners to facilitate the transaction and ensure we earn adequate returns. These merchant fees are based on the value of the goods purchased from our retail partners, the consumer&#8217;s credit risk and the terms of our bank partners' related product offering. These fees are recognized upon completion of our services, which coincides with the funding of the loan by our bank partners, in Consumer loans, including past due fees on our condensed consolidated statements of income. These merchant fees often offset the negative impact of the initial acquisition of the underlying receivable. As such, it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> always necessary for us to collect the aggregate unpaid gross balance of the underlying receivable to achieve desired returns.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-indent: 36pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
